fullPassage: Hughie is a charming young man who has achieved everything except making money. He is in love with Laura Merton, the daughter of a retired colonel. Laura loves him sincerely, but the Colonel won't let them marry until Hughie has 10,000 pounds. One day, Hughie dropped by to see his friend Alan Trevor, a painter. He was adding the finishing touches to a painting of a beggar. In the studio, the beggar himself was standing on a raised platform. He was an old man with a very pitiful face. His clothes were old and worn out. "Poor old man!" said Hughie. "How unfortunate he looks! But I suppose, for you painters, his face is his fortune?" "Certainly," replied Alan, "you wouldn't want a beggar to look happy, would you?" "How much does a model get for sitting?" asked Hughie. "A shilling an hour," answered Alan. "And how much do you get for your picture, Alan?" asked Hughie. "Oh, for this I get two thousand!" "Pounds?" "Guineas. Painters, poets, and doctors always get guineas." "Well, I think the model should get a fair share of that," cried Hughie, laughing. He continued, "as they work just as hard as you do." "Nonsense, nonsense! Look at the effort it takes to draw and paint and stand in front of the canvas all day! You mustn't talk. I'm very busy. Keep quiet," said Alan. After a while, the servant came in and told Alan that the frame-maker wanted to see him. Alan said, "I will be back in a moment," as he went out. The old beggar took advantage of Alan's absence to rest for a moment on a chair. He looked so sad and lonely. Hughie couldn't help pitying him and felt his own pockets to see what money he had. All he could find, however, was a few coins. "Poor old fellow, he wants them more than I do, but it means no carriage for two weeks," he thought to himself. He walked across the studio and put the coins into the beggar's hand. The old man was surprised and smiled faintly. "Thank you, sir," he said. Then Alan arrived, and Hughie said goodbye, blushing a little at what he had done. Hughie spent the day with Laura, received a gentle scolding for his actions, and had to walk home. That night he walked into the Palette Club at about eleven o'clock and found Alan sitting alone. Hughie asked, "Hey, Alan! Have you got that picture finished?" and Alan replied, "Finished and framed!" Then, Alan continued, "And by the way, that old model you saw is quite devoted to you. He wanted to know who you are, where you live, and what your prospects are." "My dear Alan," cried Hughie, "I shall probably find him waiting for me when I go home. Poor old man! I wish I could do something for him. I have some old clothes at home — do you think he would like any of them? His clothes were worn, falling to pieces." "But he looks wonderful in them," said Alan. "What you call worn clothes I call romance. I find them romantic and appealing. However, I'll tell him about your offer." When Hughie commented seriously, "You painters are heartless," Alan replied, "An artist's heart is his head. Our job is to show the world as we see it, not to reform it as we know it. Now tell me how Laura is. The old model was quite interested in her." "You don't mean to say you talked to him about her?" said Hughie. "Sure I did. He knows all about the Colonel, Laura, and the 10,000 pounds," replied Alan. "You told that old beggar all my private affairs?" cried Hughie, looking very red and angry. "My dear boy," said Alan, smiling, "that old beggar, as you call him, is one of the richest men in Europe. He is Baron Hausberg. He is a great friend of mine, buys all my pictures, and asked me a month ago to paint him as a beggar." "Baron Hausberg!" cried Hughie, feeling embarrassed. "Good heavens! I gave him some coins," he said, sinking into an armchair. "What? You gave him coins?" cried Alan, bursting into laughter. He went on, "Well, it never occurred to me that you would distribute money in that way. Besides, when you came in, I didn't know if Hausberg would like his name mentioned. You know he wasn't in full dress." "Oh no, what did I do? The best thing I can do is to go to bed, and, my dear Alan, you mustn't tell anyone," said Hughie, and he went home, feeling very unhappy. The next morning, when Hughie was having breakfast, an old gentleman visited his house. The man said, "I have come from Baron Hausberg," and continued, "The Baron ...." Hughie interrupted, "I beg, sir, that you will offer him my sincerest apologies." Then, with a smile, the old gentleman said, "The Baron has asked me to bring you this letter," and gave Hughie a sealed envelope. On the outside was written, "A wedding present to Hughie Erskine and Laura Merton, from an old beggar," and inside was a check for 10,000 pounds. When they were married, Alan was the best man, and the Baron made a speech at the wedding. "Millionaire models," remarked Alan, "are rare enough, but model millionaires are rarer still!"

His clothes were old and worn out. "Poor old man!" said Hughie. "How unfortunate he looks! But I suppose, for you painters, his face is his fortune?" "Certainly," replied Alan, "you wouldn't want a beggar to look happy, would you?" "How much does a model get for sitting?" asked Hughie. "A shilling an hour," answered Alan. "And how much do you get for your picture, Alan?" asked Hughie. "Oh, for this I get two thousand!" "Pounds?" "Guineas. Painters, poets, and doctors always get guineas." "Well, I think the model should get a fair share of that," cried Hughie, laughing. He continued, "as they work just as hard as you do." "Nonsense, nonsense! Look at the effort it takes to draw and paint and stand in front of the canvas all day! You mustn't talk. I'm very busy.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 이야기 도입부 사실 확인.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 본문 'Hughie is a charming young man who has achieved everything except making money' 일치

❌ ② 본문 'the daughter of a retired colonel. Laura loves him sincerely' 일치

❌ ③ 본문 'a painting of a beggar. In the studio, the beggar himself was standing on a raised platform' 일치

✅ ④ 여기가 정답(일치하지 않는 것)! 모델도 공정한 몫을 받아야 한다고 주장한 사람은 청년(Hughie)이고, 화가(Alan)는 'Nonsense, nonsense!'라며 반대했어요. 주장한 사람이 뒤바뀌어 불일치 ←정답
det.tip: 모델이 공정한 몫을 받아야 한다는 말은 청년의 말, 화가는 반대했습니다.

ch: 주인공 청년은 돈 버는 것을 빼면 거의 모든 것을 이룬 매력적인 젊은이이다.
그가 사랑하는 여인은 은퇴한 대령의 딸이며 그를 진심으로 사랑한다.
그 화가는 단상 위에 선 거지를 모델로 그림을 그리고 있었다.
그 화가는 모델도 자신만큼 보수를 받아야 한다고 청년에게 주장했다.

questions.passage: "You told that old beggar all my private affairs?" cried Hughie, looking very red and angry. "My dear boy," said Alan, smiling, "that old beggar, as you call him, is one of the richest men in Europe. He is Baron Hausberg. He is a great friend of mine, buys all my pictures, and asked me a month ago to paint him as a beggar." "Baron Hausberg!" cried Hughie, feeling embarrassed. "Good heavens! I gave him some coins," he said, sinking into an armchair. "What? You gave him coins?" cried Alan, bursting into laughter. He went on, "Well, it never occurred to me that you would distribute money in that way. Besides, when you came in, I didn't know if Hausberg would like his name mentioned. You know he wasn't in full dress." "Oh no, what did I do? The best thing I can do is to go to bed, and, my dear Alan, you mustn't tell anyone," said Hughie, and he went home, feeling very unhappy. The next morning, when Hughie was having breakfast, an old gentleman visited his house. The man said, "I have come from Baron Hausberg," and continued, "The Baron ...." Hughie interrupted, "I beg, sir, that you will offer him my sincerest apologies." Then, with a smile, the old gentleman said, "The Baron has asked me to bring you this letter," and gave Hughie a sealed envelope. On the outside was written, "A wedding present to Hughie Erskine and Laura Merton, from an old beggar," and inside was a check for 10,000 pounds. When they were married, Alan was the best man, and the Baron made a speech at the wedding.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: 이야기 결말의 반전.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 본문 'that old beggar, as you call him, is one of the richest men in Europe. He is Baron Hausberg'와 일치 ←정답

❌ ② 남작에게 청년(Hughie)의 사적인 일을 말한 사람은 화가(Alan)다. 청년은 'You told that old beggar all my private affairs?'라며 화냈으므로 불일치

❌ ③ 남작은 화를 낸 것이 아니라 결혼 선물로 수표를 보냈다. 불일치

❌ ④ 본문 'inside was a check for 10,000 pounds'에서 초상화가 아니라 1만 파운드짜리 수표를 보냈다. 불일치
det.tip: 사실은 그 거지가 남작이었다는 것이 일치. 나머지는 본문과 어긋납니다.

ch: 그 늙은 거지는 사실 유럽 최고 부자 중 한 명인 남작이었다.
주인공 청년은 남작에게 자신의 사적인 일을 직접 모두 이야기했다.
남작은 청년의 무례함에 화가 나 두 사람의 결혼을 반대했다.
남작은 결혼 선물로 청년에게 자신의 초상화 한 점을 보냈다.

questions.passage: The next morning, when Hughie was ①<u>having</u> breakfast, an old gentleman visited his house. The man said, "I have come from Baron Hausberg," and continued, "The Baron ...." Hughie interrupted, "I beg, sir, that you will offer him my sincerest apologies." Then, with a smile, the old gentleman said, "The Baron has asked me to bring you this letter," and gave Hughie a sealed envelope. On the outside was ②<u>writing</u>, "A wedding present to Hughie Erskine and Laura Merton, from an old beggar," and inside was a check for 10,000 pounds. When they were ③<u>married</u>, Alan was the best man, and the Baron made a speech at the wedding. "Millionaire models," ④<u>remarked</u> Alan, "are rare enough, but model millionaires are rarer still!"
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② writing → written: 수동태 was + 과거분사이므로 was written
det.analysis:
① having: 'when Hughie was having breakfast'에서 'be동사 + V-ing'의 과거진행형이라 having이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② writing → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'On the outside was ___, "A wedding present ~"'는 '겉면에 ~라고 쓰여 있었다'라는 수동의 의미예요. 'be동사 + 과거분사'의 수동태라 written으로 써야 하고, writing(현재분사)은 능동이라 틀려요. ❌ writing은 틀림 ←정답

③ married: 'When they were married'에서 '결혼하게 되었을 때'라는 수동 표현이라 과거분사 married가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

④ remarked: ''Millionaire models,' remarked Alan'에서 '말했다'라는 과거시제 remarked가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: 수동태 was + 과거분사: was written(쓰여 있었다)

questions.passage: "What you call worn clothes I call romance. I find them romantic and appealing. However, I'll tell him about your offer." When Hughie commented seriously, "You painters are heartless," Alan replied, "An artist's heart is his head.

det.analysis: 구문 분석: 주어 Hughie에 이어지는 동사는 spend, received, had로 and에 의해 병렬 연결돼요. received와 had가 모두 과거시제이므로 spend도 과거시제 spent로 맞춰야 해요. spend-spent-spent로 변하는 불규칙 동사예요. 'Hughie는 하루를 보냈고(spent), 꾸지람을 들었고, 걸어가야 했다'로 해석돼요.

사람을 겉모습(차림새)만으로 함부로 판단해서는 안 된다.

questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"그는 나보다 그것(돈)을 더 원한다." (7단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) I, do, he, more, than, them, wants 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 7단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: he wants them more than I do
det.analysis:
주어는 he, 동사는 현재시제 wants(3인칭 단수)예요: he + wants.

목적어 '그것(동전)'은 them이에요: he wants them.

'~보다 더'는 비교 표현 more than으로 나타내요: more than.

비교 대상 '나(는)'는 I이고, 반복을 피하려고 대동사 do를 써요(= more than I want them): than + I + do.

순서대로 이으면 he / wants / them / more / than / I / do.
det.tip: 비교구문 more than + 주어 + 대동사(do): he wants them more than I do
